text:
raj: Heads-up — noticed spike in duplicate resume attempts for WS sessions this morning, looks correlated with console 'snooze' for backpressure alerts. Some tenants got 2-3 resume attempts in <2s and we billed each as separate streams.
sam: Oof. Any logs showing resume_token reuse vs new session creation?
raj: Pasting a snippet from the edge proxy logs:
```
2026-03-20T07:12:11Z INFO session_resume token=abc123 tenant=acme conn_id=42 route=us-west proxy=gw-7
2026-03-20T07:12:11Z WARN session_drop conn_id=41 reason=kicked_by_quota
2026-03-20T07:12:12Z INFO session_new token=abc123 tenant=acme conn_id=43 route=us-west proxy=gw-7
2026-03-20T07:12:12Z INFO billing_charge tenant=acme event=stream_start amount=0.001
```
sam: So same token shows up on conn 42 then conn 43; proxy didn't treat resume as idempotent because stale lease flag was cleared.
elle: Is this the same code path that the resume-window heuristic uses? We added a short grace window to allow session migration, but we also have a console toggle that silences backpressure alerts — could that be causing autoscaler to stop shedding connections and trigger rapid reconnects?
maria: The console 'snooze' only suppresses alerts, it shouldn't change routing decisions. But I noticed we wire a 'maintenance mode' flag thatops can check; if someone used the quick UI to silence alerts they might have accidentally toggled maintenance for a route in the same modal — bad UX.
raj: I saw a maintenance flag flip around the same time in audit logs: `route_maintenance: true` for route=us-west by user=ops-tilly.
sam: If maintenance changes proxy behavior (disable backpressure shedding), then overloaded hosts will drop sessions and clients try resume -> duplicate resume tokens and double billing.
elle: Two linked problems then: UX allows accidental maintenance toggle next to snooze, and resume idempotency isn't robust when proxies flip shedding behavior. We should short-term rate-limit resume attempts per token at the control plane to avoid double billing.
observability-bot: FYI: added metric counter `resume_attempts_by_token` and an alert (non-snoozed) for >5 attempts/min for same token across proxies. See dashboard: https://console/redwood/d/streaming/resume-attempts
maria: Agree with control-plane rate limiter. Also let's make console modal separate actions (snooze vs maintenance) and add a confirmation for maintenance.
sam: For runtime fix: treat resume_token as idempotent for N seconds after first seen, reject or merge subsequent resume within that window and return a special 409-like payload so client doesn't bill twice.
raj: Can we also retroactively credit customers for obviously duplicated charges? I can compile a tenant list if we detect token reuse with multiple billing_events within 5s.
elle: Yes, add a reconciliation job that searches billing_events joined to resume_attempts_by_token and flags potential duplicates.
maria: I'll own the console UX change. @sam or @elle can you draft the runtime patch and a short rollout plan? We need a canary that rejects duplicate resume harmlessly.
sam: I'll prototype the token idempotency window today. Plan: 1) control-plane rate limiter 2) runtime reject-with-merge on canary 3) dashboard & reconciliation job. Canary target: 10% of us-west.
raj: Thanks — also adding postmortem placeholder just in case. I'll ping billing to prepare credits if we confirm duplicates.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started for runtime change (gw-immutable-2026-03-20-rc1) :rocket:
maria: UX PR drafted: https://git/redwood/console/pull/542 — separates snooze & maintenance, adds confirmation and tooltip. Will request review from @ux.
elle: Observability: can you add a small panel showing maintenance toggles alongside resume spikes? makes debugging easier.
observability-bot: Added panel to streaming/resume dashboard and annotated timeframe 2026-03-20T07:10-07:20 for the spike.
raj: Great — we should aim for a shortie runbook entry: what to check (maintenance flag, resume_attempts_by_token, billing events) and mitigation steps (enable idempotency canary, apply transient credits). I'll draft it.
sam: Will follow up in the thread when prototype is up. :thumbsup:
